description: What InternetData knows about one autonomous system, by its number: its operator, country, registry, allocation date and domain, the kind of network it runs, how many IPv4 addresses and prefixes it announces with their RPKI counts, its ASN Whois record, its rank and whether it is Tier 1, the AS numbers it gets transit from, peers with and provides transit to, how many domains it hosts with the most popular, and the prefixes it announces in global BGP with their RPKI status. The prefixes and each list of AS numbers hold their first 100, the AS numbers ascending, with `truncated` giving the total where there are more. An AS no database knows comes back as its number with empty values. Always read `coverage.note` before concluding anything from a field that is not in the result.
name: lookup_asn

coverage.description: Which datasets this result covered. Read `note` before interpreting any absent field.

result.description: What every database says about one AS.

cap_reached.description: On every answer to a key on a paid plan, and on no other: `false` while the answer has every field, `true` once its organization's overage cap is reached and the answer has Unlimited's. Lookups answered past the cap are not billed; raising or removing the cap in Billing turns it `false` again.

country.description: The country its registry assigned it to.

downstreams.description: Those AS numbers, ascending, up to 20000. Paid plans and the trial.

hosted_domains.description: From ASN Hosted Domains: how many registered domains the AS hosts, and the 10 most popular. Its database lists up to 1,000 an AS. Paid plans and the trial.

domains.description: Up to 10 of them, the most popular first; `[]` when none does.

total.description: How many registered domains resolve to an address the AS announces.

num_downstreams.description: How many AS numbers it provides transit to. Paid plans and the trial.

num_ips.description: IPv4 addresses it announces. Paid plans and the trial.

num_peers.description: How many AS numbers it exchanges its own and its customers' routes with. Paid plans and the trial.

num_prefixes4.description: IPv4 prefixes it announces. Paid plans and the trial.

num_prefixes6.description: IPv6 prefixes it announces. Paid plans and the trial.

num_upstreams.description: How many AS numbers it gets transit from. Paid plans and the trial.

peers.description: Those AS numbers, ascending, up to 20000. Paid plans and the trial.

prefixes.description: What it announces, IPv4 then IPv6, up to 20000 a family. Paid plans and the trial.

first_seen.description: The first day BGP Route saw it.

size.description: IPv4 addresses it covers; 0 for IPv6.

rank.description: Its rank in ASN Extended, by customer cone, 1 the largest; `0` for an AS seen in no AS path. Paid plans and the trial.

rpki_invalid.description: Invalid. Paid plans and the trial.

rpki_not_found.description: With no RPKI record. Paid plans and the trial.

rpki_valid.description: Its announcements RPKI calls valid. Paid plans and the trial.

tier1.description: Whether it is one of the transit-free networks at the top of the hierarchy, which get transit from no one and peer with each other. Paid plans and the trial.

trial_expired.description: On every answer to a key on the free plan, and on no other: `false` while its organization's trial of every field lasts, `true` once the answer has Unlimited's fields.

type.description: The kind of network it runs. Paid plans and the trial.

upstreams.description: Those AS numbers, ascending, up to 20000. Paid plans and the trial.

whois.description: Its ASN Whois record, every column, empty where the registry states nothing. Paid plans and the trial.

truncated.description: Present only when the answer was cut short: for each list it cut, how many entries it carries and how many there are, and where to get them all.

title: Look up an AS
